name: Rewiring America (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: shares of the result at the defaults. The public money won for US households, their net gain and the asthma averted (98.6%) are in the United States; the tonnes (1.4%) spare people everywhere, spread by world population.
summary: Rewiring America works to electrify American homes: it designed the Inflation Reduction Act's home-electrification rebates and runs free tools and coaching that help households switch to heat pumps and other electric appliances ($22.7M spent in 2024, its first year filing on its own after leaving the Windward Fund). This model counts its share of the law's home-energy provisions (rebates and home credits) won in 2021-2024 and the households its tools and coaches bring to switch sooner, against a typical year's spending in that period: the tonnes they cut, the public money won for households, the households' own net gain or loss from switching and cleaner indoor air where a gas stove goes. At the defaults that is {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000, because it counts the law's $8.8 billion of home-energy rebates, mostly for low- and moderate-income homes, and three years of larger home credits as public money won, valued by the site's rule for aid won as the recipients' gain less the taxpayers' cost, at its large share of the advocacy behind the rebates it designed (35%): nearly all of the result, the tonnes giving about 3% of it; the larger home credits, claimed mostly by better-off households, count slightly below zero. The households the law's subsidies tipped into switching lose a little on it before the subsidy (our guess, −$120 a year each), which alone puts the tonnes' part slightly below zero. The biggest uncertainties are the shared missing-data step, advocacy's share of a won policy, the next-dollar figure and Rewiring America's share of the advocacy behind the rebates; since May 2026 the rebates no longer pay for switching from gas, so less of them will be paid. Both branches are discounted for missing data, since nothing is measured for its work.

source.title: Canary Media (2022), Climate bill could spur market transformation in home electrification (16 August 2022)
source.quote: Rewiring America forecasts that the rebates could enable roughly 1 million households to switch to all-electric power

rows.explainer: The provisions Rewiring America worked on: the $4.5B electrification rebates (HEEHRA, now HEAR), the $4.3B efficiency rebates (HOMES) and the larger home-improvement and home clean-energy credits (25C, 25D). Rewiring America forecast that the rebates could help about 1 million households go all-electric (Canary Media), about 3 million tonnes a year at the shared per-home figure once all are done; the credits' extra heat pumps and rooftop solar might add 10 to 20 million tonnes a year by 2030, our guess, since no projection we found splits the law's cut by provision. That is 13 to 23 million of the law's projected 900 million (facts: climate.ira_tco2e_per_year_2030): 2% (1% to 5%), our judgment; buildings are a small part of every model's projection, which is mostly power and vehicles. The law's other provisions that follow Rewiring America's asks are left out: the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund's low-income part (its awards, its affiliate's among them, were frozen and terminated in 2025, so almost nothing is delivered) and $500M of Defense Production Act money for heat-pump factories (small beside the rebates and credits).

source.title: Allcott & Rogers (2014), The short-run and long-run effects of behavioral interventions: experimental evidence from energy conservation, American Economic Review 104(10): 3003-3037
source.note: Reference class: Opower's home energy reports, randomised across hundreds of thousands of homes, cut electricity use by about 2%, mostly through small habits rather than new equipment.

rows.explainer: Of the households who use the calculator or planner, how many make a switch worth a heat pump's tonnes (a heat pump, or a heat-pump water heater, induction stove and the like adding up to one) sooner than they would have without them. No one has measured it: the users are mostly already interested, and information alone moves few home-energy decisions (home energy reports cut use by about 2% in randomised trials, mostly through habits, Allcott & Rogers 2014). 1.5% (0.3% to 5%), our judgment; the years sooner are a row below.

rows.label: Years sooner a household switches because of the tools
rows.explainer: A switch made sooner counts only until the household would have switched anyway, at its next replacement or as gas gets dearer and heat pumps cheaper. A furnace lasts 15-20 years and a heat pump about 15, so a switch made at a breakdown that would otherwise have gone back to gas is brought forward by up to a heat pump's life; one a few years ahead of plan by less. 7 years (3 to 15), our judgment.

rows.label: Years from using the tools until the switch is installed
rows.explainer: Planning, quotes and installation. Reference class: the UK's Boiler Upgrade Scheme gives an installer three months from the grant voucher to fit an air-source heat pump (The Boiler Upgrade Scheme (England and Wales) Regulations 2022, regulation 15(2)), and a household first spends weeks to months comparing options and getting quotes; a panel upgrade or ductwork adds more. Half a year (a quarter to a year and a half), our judgment.

rows.label: The rebates: Rewiring America's share of the advocacy behind them

source.title: Canary Media (2022), Climate bill could spur market transformation in home electrification (16 August 2022)
source.quote: Based on a Rewiring America plan

rows.explainer: The electrification rebates were built on Rewiring America's own plan and it was their leading advocate; the efficiency rebates (HOMES) had long-standing efficiency backers, and both passed inside a law that many more groups pushed. 35% (15% to 60%), our judgment.

rows.label: The larger home credits: Rewiring America's share of the advocacy behind them
rows.explainer: Rewiring America pressed for the heat-pump part of the home-improvement credit (25C), but the residential clean energy credit (25D), three-quarters of the money, was mainly the rooftop-solar industry's ask, renewed several times before. 10% (3% to 25%), our judgment.

rows.label: The rebates' share of the home provisions' tonnes
rows.explainer: About 3 of the provisions' 18 million tonnes a year come from the rebates and the rest from the credits (ira_household_share's explainer): 17% (10% to 30%), our judgment.

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): governments' budgets and enforcement, companies' compliance, the use others make of research. The charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work. Fixed.

rows.label: Inflation Reduction Act's home-energy provisions: credit share used
rows.explainer: The share among co-advocates times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: Home-energy provisions' delivered share relative to the whole law's

source.title: US Internal Revenue Service (2025), FAQs for modification of sections 25C, 25D, 25E, 30C, 30D, 45L, 45W and 179D under Public Law 119-21 (the One, Big, Beautiful Bill)
source.note: The 2025 budget law ends the 25C credit for property placed in service after 31 December 2025, and 25D on the same date. DOE's revised rebate guidance (29 May 2026, reported by Utility Dive, https://www.utilitydive.com/news/doe-issues-guidance-gas-electric-appliance-rebate/821720/) ends the electrification rebates for replacing fossil fuel-fired appliances.

rows.explainer: The 2025 budget law ended both home credits after 2025, ten years early, and DOE's revised guidance of May 2026 (Utility Dive) ended the electrification rebates for households replacing gas or other fossil equipment, so the rebates' tonnes now come only from electric-to-electric upgrades and new homes, while states rework and resubmit their programmes. The whole law also kept less (its power credits end for projects begun after 2027), but the home provisions lost more of theirs: 0.7 (0.35 to 1.1) of the law's own delivered share, our judgment.

rows.label: Inflation Reduction Act's home-energy provisions: share of their tonnes delivered
rows.explainer: The shared delivered share of the law (facts: climate.ira_delivered_share, 35%) times the home provisions' relative row: about 28%.

rows.label: Tools and coaching: share of their switches not already in the law's projected tonnes
rows.explainer: The years sooner already say what the households would have done without the tools. What remains is overlap with the law's branch: its projection assumes households take up its credits and rebates, and a tool that helps a household claim them partly delivers that projected uptake, counted there at Rewiring America's share. 80% (60% to 100%), our judgment.

rows.label: Tools and coaching: Rewiring America's share of the resources behind the switches
rows.explainer: A switch the tools brought sooner also took a contractor's quote and sales effort, the rebate and utility programmes' outreach and, for coaches, their own volunteer time. 50% (20% to 80%), our judgment, of which the tools' own makers take the share below.

source.quote: negotiated with manufacturers to lower the cost of heat pumps for households by 40 percent

rows.explainer: The rest of the work, each a share of the tonnes counted: heat-pump prices it negotiated with manufacturers for its programmes and a free database of 3,500 incentives that utilities and states build on, which may speed switches beyond its own users, 10%; free technical analyses for states and cities applying for funds and for utility programmes and rates, and its research (the health and jobs reports), 7%; community demonstration projects in five places, 3%. 20% (5% to 50%), our judgment. The households' own gains and costs and cleaner indoor air are counted in their own units below. The public money is the law's alone; the other work wins none of it, so the share applies to the tonnes only.

rows.label: The law's households: net gain a year from switching, before incentives (bills saved less the extra equipment's yearly cost)

source.title: American Public Power Association (2024), Benefits of heat pumps detailed in new NREL report (on Wilson et al. 2024, Joule)
source.quote: with median savings of $300 to $650 a year
source.note: For homes heated with electricity, fuel oil or propane that have air conditioning, 92% to 100% would see lower bills; across all homes 62% to 95%, depending on the heat pump's efficiency; high installation costs make heat pumps 'financially feasible for a smaller portion of households'.

rows.explainer: What a heat-pump household the law brought to switch gains or loses itself: bills saved less the heat pump's extra cost over a furnace and air conditioner, spread over its life, at prices before incentives (the incentives themselves are counted below as public money won: recipients' gain less taxpayers' cost). The law's tonnes come from switches its subsidies caused, and for a household a subsidy tips into switching that net is between minus the subsidy and zero: a $2,000 credit is about $170 a year over 15 years at 4%, an $8,000 electrification rebate about $700. Most of these households claim the credits; some homes gain even unsubsidised (bills fall by a median $300-650 a year in homes heated with electricity, oil or propane, Wilson et al. 2024) but those would mostly have switched anyway. About half the subsidy, weighted to the credits: −$120 a year per household (−$350 to +$50), our judgment, in 2024 dollars.

rows.label: Tool-led households: net gain a year from switching sooner, before incentives

source.title: American Public Power Association (2024), Benefits of heat pumps detailed in new NREL report (on Wilson et al. 2024, Joule)
source.quote: with median savings of $300 to $650 a year
source.note: For homes heated with electricity, fuel oil or propane that have air conditioning, 92% to 100% would see lower bills; across all homes 62% to 95%, depending on the heat pump's efficiency; high installation costs make heat pumps 'financially feasible for a smaller portion of households'.

rows.explainer: A household the tools bring to switch sooner chose to with the tool's figures for its own home in hand, often finding savings it didn't know of: on average it gains, even with the incentives (transfers) left out, though gas-heated homes may pay more. $50 a year (−$150 to +$300), our judgment, in 2024 dollars, anchored on Wilson et al.'s bill savings and the heat pump's extra cost.

rows.label: The law's households: value of the net gain, units of value per household-year
rows.explainer: The shared value of consumption: the gain over the household's yearly spending (US Consumer Expenditure Survey per person, facts: united_states.ce_expenditure_per_person_2024, × the shared US household size) through ln, per person, × the shared value of a doubled consumption.

rows.label: Tool-led households: value of the net gain, units of value per household-year
rows.explainer: As for the law's households.

rows.label: The law's home provisions: share of their tonnes from heat-pump switches
rows.explainer: The households' net gain and the gas stoves follow heat-pump switches; the provisions' other tonnes come from rooftop solar (25D, which held three-quarters of the credits' $8.4B claimed for 2023) and insulation and efficiency (HOMES). Solar and insulation households are left out of the net gain: their panels and insulation are not a heat pump's trade of equipment cost against bills, and no figure we found gives their unsubsidised net. 60% (40% to 85%), our judgment: solar cuts more tonnes per dollar of credit than heat pumps do, but heat pumps hold the rebates and most of the efficiency credit.

rows.label: Side effect: share of the switches counted that replace a gas stove
rows.explainer: The switches counted are mostly heating and water heating; some households also replace a gas stove with induction, which the rebates pay for ($840) and the tools cover. 15% (5% to 35%), our judgment: about a third of US homes cook with gas, and a stove is usually the last appliance switched.

rows.explainer: The attributable share rests on observational odds ratios, not trials; critics argue confounding (older, poorer housing) explains part of it, and swapping a stove removes the exposure only going forward. 0.5 (0.2 to 1), our judgment.

rows.label: Healthy years a year gained per gas stove replaced
rows.explainer: Each case averted is a year without asthma at GBD 2019's weight for partially controlled asthma (facts: gbd_disability_weights.asthma_partially_controlled, 0.036), between controlled (0.015) and uncontrolled (0.133), our choice for a typical child's case; asthma deaths in children are rare and left out.

rows.label: The law's home-electrification rebates (HEEHRA, now HEAR)
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate.ira_home_electrification_rebates_usd, $4.5 billion): point-of-sale rebates for low- and moderate-income homes.

rows.label: The law's whole-home efficiency rebates (HOMES)
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate.ira_home_efficiency_rebates_usd, $4.3 billion).

rows.label: Share of the rebate money that reaches households
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate.ira_home_rebates_paid_share, {{row:rebate_paid_share}}).

rows.label: Years from the law (2022) to the middle of the rebates' payouts
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate.ira_home_rebates_years_until_paid, {{row:rebate_years_until_paid}} years). The rebates are a fixed sum and count once.

rows.label: Rebate recipients' consumption per person, relative to the US survey average
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate.ira_home_rebates_recipient_consumption_ratio, 0.6).

rows.label: The law's increase in the two home credits (25C, 25D), tax year 2023
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate.ira_home_credits_increment_2023_usd, $3.8 billion).

rows.label: The law's increase in the two home credits, a year in 2024-2025
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate.ira_home_credits_increment_2024_2025_usd_per_year, $8.4 billion a year).

rows.label: Years the larger home credits paid (2023-2025)
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate.ira_home_credits_years, 3): from 2023 until the 2025 budget law ended both.

rows.label: Years from the law (2022) until the first larger credits are claimed
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate.ira_home_credits_years_until_paid, {{row:credit_years_until_paid}} years).

rows.label: Credit claimants' consumption per person, relative to the US survey average
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: climate.ira_home_credits_recipient_consumption_ratio, 1.3).

rows.label: ln(consumption) given up by taxpayers per dollar of federal money
rows.explainer: The shared cost of public money (facts: public_funds.mcpf, 1.2) over how federal taxes fall (public_funds.us_federal_payer_multiple, 1.4) times the household survey's consumption per person (the recipients' scale: one consumption scale for US public money, docs/normalization.md 2.14).

rows.label: The rebates: recipients' gain less taxpayers' cost, units of value
rows.explainer: A dollar to a household adds about 1 ÷ its consumption per person to ln consumption, and costs the taxpayers the payer row: the difference × the shared value of a doubled consumption, discounted to the middle of the payouts. The rebates are a fixed sum, so they count once, not for the years a won reform counts.

rows.label: Years of the larger credits counted (the shared years a won reform counts, at most the years they paid)
The larger credits: claimants' gain less taxpayers' cost, units of value
rows.explainer: The larger credits were a yearly stream won with the law, so like any won policy's yearly benefit they count the shared years a won reform counts, here at most the three years they paid: 2023's increase in the first year, 2024-2025's in each later one, discounted year by year from the first claims, each dollar valued as the claimants' gain less the taxpayers' cost.

rows.label: Public money won for households, units of value per year of the period (after the law's branch steps)
rows.formula: (rebate_uov * rebate_attribution_share_shared + credit_uov * credit_attribution_share_shared) * mobiliser_share * p_success * ira_counterfactual_adj * missing_data_adj / period_years
rows.explainer: The law's branch steps for the money: advocacy's share of the win, what wouldn't have come anyway, Rewiring America's share of the advocacy behind each (the rebates' and the credits' own) and the missing-data step, spread over the period's four years. The tonnes' evidence and delivery steps are left out: the money is a sum in the statute and the claims Treasury counted, its delivery in the paid share. At the mobiliser's share, as the branch's tonnes are (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: Households' money: net gain from switching and public money won, units of value per year of the period
rows.formula: (ira_downstream_per_year * ira_total_adj * ira_heat_pump_share_of_tonnes * ira_uov_per_household_year + tools_downstream * tools_total_adj * tools_uov_per_household_year) / tonnes_per_household_year + ira_transfer_uov_per_year
rows.explainer: Each branch's heat-pump switches are its heat-pump tonnes over the per-home cut, counted over the same discounted years and with the same adjustments as the tonnes, times the value of a household-year's net gain; plus the public money won.

rows.label: Cleaner indoor air, healthy years per year of the period (after each branch's adjustments)
rows.formula: (ira_downstream_per_year * ira_total_adj * ira_heat_pump_share_of_tonnes + tools_downstream * tools_total_adj) / tonnes_per_household_year * stove_share_of_switches * asthma_dalys_per_stove_home_year
rows.explainer: The heat-pump switches counted, over the same discounted years and adjustments as the tonnes, × the share replacing a gas stove × the healthy years a stove replaced gains a year.

rows.label: Share of these tonnes that are methane
rows.explainer: Gas a home stops burning also stops leaking upstream (facts: climate.us_home_electrification_methane_share, {{row:methane_share}}): both branches' tonnes come from homes electrified. The shared conversion values it by methane's own, earlier warming and ozone.

rows.label: Share of these tonnes from burning less fossil fuel near people
rows.explainer: Every tonne here except the upstream methane is gas, oil or propane no longer burned in homes, net of the extra power plants' fuel.

rows.label: Smoke per tonne of these cuts, relative to the fossil-fuel average
rows.explainer: The shared factor for tonnes from US homes electrified (facts: climate.us_home_electrification_smoke_factor, 0.02): gas no longer burned at ground level near people, less the extra power plants' mostly scrubbed smoke. The law's branch also holds some rooftop solar (25D), whose smoke is US power's (0.013, inside the range).

rows.label: Air pollution these tonnes cut, relative to an average fossil-fuel tonne
rows.explainer: Read by the tco2e unit's conversion (docs/normalization.md 2.5).

rows.label: Air-pollution deaths averted per tonne, counted directly (none here)
rows.explainer: No source counts deaths beside these tonnes; their smoke is in air_pollution_weight, so nothing is counted twice.

rows.label: Households' net gain, in tonnes of CO₂e
rows.formula: uov_bridged / (($deaths_per_tco2e * $climate_heat_share * ((1 - methane_share) * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -$climate_heat_death_delay + methane_share * @climate.methane_heat_deaths_vs_co2 * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -@climate.methane_heat_death_delay) * (1 + $side_effect_weight * @climate.nondeath_damages_vs_deaths) * (@death_ages.heat_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.heat_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.heat_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.heat_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74) + ($deaths_per_tco2e * (1 - $climate_heat_share) * air_pollution_weight + extra_deaths_per_tco2e + methane_share * @climate.ozone_deaths_per_tco2e_methane / (1 + ln(1 + $discount_rate) * @climate.methane_lifetime_years)) * (@death_ages.air_pollution_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74)) * $life_value_multiplier)
rows.explainer: The households' gain enters the tonnes only through the site's fixed bridge (docs/normalization.md 2.6): it moves with the value of consumption, not with the climate sliders.

rows.label: Cleaner indoor air, in tonnes of CO₂e
rows.formula: dalys_bridged * ($uov_per_daly) / (($deaths_per_tco2e * $climate_heat_share * ((1 - methane_share) * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -$climate_heat_death_delay + methane_share * @climate.methane_heat_deaths_vs_co2 * (1 + $discount_rate) ^ -@climate.methane_heat_death_delay) * (1 + $side_effect_weight * @climate.nondeath_damages_vs_deaths) * (@death_ages.heat_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.heat_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.heat_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.heat_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74) + ($deaths_per_tco2e * (1 - $climate_heat_share) * air_pollution_weight + extra_deaths_per_tco2e + methane_share * @climate.ozone_deaths_per_tco2e_methane / (1 + ln(1 + $discount_rate) * @climate.methane_lifetime_years)) * (@death_ages.air_pollution_share_under5 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_under5 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_5_14 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_5_14 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_15_49 * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_15_49 + @death_ages.air_pollution_share_50plus * @moral_weights.uov_per_death_age_50_74)) * $life_value_multiplier)
rows.explainer: The asthma averted enters the tonnes only through the site's fixed bridge (docs/normalization.md 2.6): it moves with the value of a healthy year, not with the climate sliders.

rows.label: Tonnes of CO₂e averted per year of the period
rows.formula: (ira_downstream_per_year * ira_total_adj + tools_downstream * tools_total_adj) * (1 + unmodelled_benefits_adj) + tco2e_from_uov + tco2e_from_daly
rows.explainer: Each branch's tonnes × its own adjustments, summed, with the other work added as a share; then the households' net gain and the cleaner indoor air, each through its bridge.
